title: Adaptive timeout pruning for partial streams and resource reclamation
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: When clients disconnect or stall during an in-progress streaming generation, the runtime can retain partial generation state (prefix cache, KV cache reservations, lease ownership) longer than necessary, tying up GPU memory and slots and increasing tail-latency for other requests. Current heuristics use a fixed idle timeout and a simple orphan scan job which often either reclaims too aggressively (causing resumed clients to lose context) or too lazily (wasting capacity).

Goal: Implement an adaptive timeout and pruning system that: (1) classifies partial streams by likely-resumability, (2) adjusts reclamation timers based on client history and model characteristics, (3) performs safe pruning that preserves resumption tokens when possible, and (4) provides operational signals and a console view for reclaimed partial generations. This should reduce wasted GPU memory and improve request throughput under high churn without regressing resumability for legitimate reconnects.
acceptance_criteria: Adaptive timer reduces median held-time for abandoned partial streams by >= 40% in synthetic churn workloads compared to fixed 60s timeout
Resumption success rate for clients that reconnect within 30s does not drop by more than 2% on regression test suite
KV cache and GPU slot utilization metrics show 15% improvement in 95th pct tail under mixed traffic (short-lived chat clients + long-running batch)
Console adds a 'Partial Generations' table with filter by reclaim-reason and a per-item history link
PRs merged with unit + integration tests and e2e chaos test demonstrating safe pruning during network partitions
technical_notes: Classifier features: last-client-heartbeat, average tokens/sec for this session, model family (decoder-only vs. encoder-decoder), request priority (route/token tier), presence of tool/function calls or long structured outputs
Timer policy: base_timeout = f(model_family, avg_tokens_per_sec) * decay_factor(client_reconnect_rate) with enforced min/max bounds

Safe pruning steps: try to emit final 'partial' delta to client websocket if still connected; otherwise create resumable token object with compact KV snapshot and tombstone metadata before releasing heavy GPU KV pages
Resumption token format: signed opaque token referencing compacted KV snapshot id + model_version + sequence_id; supports backward compatibility with older runtime via compatibility layer
Migration path: feature-flag behind 'adaptive-stream-pruning' with telemetry gated rollout (10% -> 50% -> 100%)
Observability hooks: emit events 'partial_held', 'partial_reclaimed', 'resumption_attempt', 'resumption_good' with tags: route, model, size_bytes, last_activity_seconds, reclaim_reason
progress_updates: 2026-02-26: Spike completed to measure held-time distribution for partial streams across p50/p95/p99. Found bimodal distribution with a long tail beyond 10 minutes for test harness clients.

2026-03-02: Prototype classifier implemented in runtime mock service (python). Initial heuristic: reduce timeout by 50% for sessions with avg_tokens_per_sec > 6 or when request contained no tool calls.

2026-03-05: Integration test harness updated to inject reconnect events; observed 30% reduction in GPU memory held-time but resumption success rate dropped by 6% for reconnects at 25-40s. Rollback of aggressive rule pending.
2026-03-08: Design review with PM and Infra: decide to add a 'soft-evict' phase that preserves compact resumable token for short reconnections, full-prune only after second-stage timeout
2026-03-10: Implemented soft-evict + token compaction; added console mock for Partial Generations. Preparing PRs for runtime and console changes. Marking tests green locally for common cases.
review_feedback: 2026-03-04 - PM (Evelyn Choi): Concern about TDs where tool/function calls include external side effects; recommend flagging such sessions as non-resumable by default.
2026-03-06 - Security (Jonas Weber): Resumption token must be HMAC-signed and TTL-limited; do not store PII in compacted snapshots. Add KMS rotation considerations.

2026-03-09 - Runtime Lead (Priya Menon): Suggest moving classifier model/features into the routing service to avoid per-GPU overhead. Also add circuit-breaker to fall back to fixed-timeouts if classifier errors.
2026-03-10 - Design (Lina Ortega): Console view should expose 'reclaim_preview' telemetry and an option to recover a reclaimed partial for internal debugging within 7 days.
next_steps: Open runtime PRs for soft-evict and resumable-token compaction (blocking: KMS signing integration)
Add e2e chaos scenario for flaky network where client reconnects after 20-90s; run against staging cluster
Create console endpoint to surface 'Partial Generations' and wire telemetry events
Coordinate rollout plan with infra and SRE: start 10% on canary cluster, monitor 'resumption_good' events
notes_for_oncall: If SLO regressions observed for latency or increased OOMs, toggle feature flag 'adaptive-stream-pruning' to off via runtime-config console
Telemetry counters to watch: partial_reclaimed_rate, resumable_token_created, resumption_success_rate, gpu_kv_held_bytes
In case of suspicious spikes in 'resumption_attempt' failures, collect the compacted snapshot id and escalate to Runtime Lead for debugging
